# Badge

> A read-only status or count pill: a hairline outline, a word, and an optional lime dot or glyph.

Part of the [Nate Mills Design System](../README.md). It is a CSS class API, not a JavaScript component, so its props are the classes and HTML attributes below. Link the stylesheets as [Getting started](../foundations/getting-started.md) shows, then add the classes. Every component: [Components](../COMPONENTS.md).

## When to use

- A status, such as "Open to work" or "In progress".
- A read-only count of something, outside a carousel.

## When not to use

- A plain label or tag: use a Chip.
- A position in a carousel: the Carousel navigation dots show it.
- Anything clickable: use a Button or a Link.

## Alternatives

- **[Chip](chip.md):** Same pill shape, different job: a badge reports a status, a chip labels. Pick by what the words do.
- **[Carousel navigation](carousel-navigation.md):** A position in a carousel is shown by its dots, never a badge.

## How to use

**Element:** `<span>`

- Put `.badge` on a `<span>` with the status word as its text.
- For the dot form, start it with `<span class="badge__dot" aria-hidden="true"></span>`; for the icon form, a Lucide glyph marked `aria-hidden="true"`.

**Classes:** `.badge`, `.badge__dot`

## Props

| Prop | Type | Allowed values | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `form` | child element | `dot`: a `<span class="badge__dot" aria-hidden="true">`; `icon`: a leading Lucide `<i data-lucide="..." aria-hidden="true">`; `plain`: words only | `plain` | What leads the word. The dot stays lime in both themes. |

## Variants

Available forms: `dot`, `icon`, `plain`. They are child elements, not modifier classes: `.badge` has no modifiers. Default form: `plain`.

## States

No interactive states: a badge is a status and never takes a click or focus.

## Invalid combinations

Options that must not be used together. Each names the props above.

| Combination | Level | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `form: dot` with `form: icon` | MUST NOT | Pick one form; two leading marks read as two signals. |
| `.badge` on a `<button>` or an `<a>` | MUST NOT | A badge reports, it never acts. |
| `form: dot` with no word beside it | MUST NOT | Colour alone reaches no screen reader. |

## Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Passes over it: a badge is not focusable. |
| Enter, Space | Do nothing: a badge takes no input. |
| Down arrow in a screen reader's browse mode (VoiceOver: VO + Right arrow) | Reads the status word. The `.badge__dot` is `aria-hidden`, so it is skipped. |

A badge reports a status and never takes input.

## Rules

| Level | Rule | Checked by |
|---|---|---|
| MUST | Give every status a word as well as the dot; colour is never the only signal (WCAG 1.4.1). | [Automated: Component-rules lint](../foundations/checks.md#component-rules-lint) |
| MUST | Mark `.badge__dot` `aria-hidden="true"`. | [Automated: Component-rules lint](../foundations/checks.md#component-rules-lint) |
| MUST NOT | Make `.badge` interactive. | [Automated: Component-rules lint](../foundations/checks.md#component-rules-lint) |

Automated checks run on natemills.me before every publish; the scripts live in the private source repository.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Use `.badge` for a read-only status or count, and give every status a word as well as a dot.
- Keep `.badge__dot` decorative and `aria-hidden`, so colour is never the only channel carrying the state.
- Send a plain label to `.chip` and leave a carousel position to its dots (`.ds-carousel-nav__dot`); `.badge` covers the middle case.
- Write a text label on every badge, because `.badge__dot` is `aria-hidden` and colour alone reaches no screen reader.

### Don't

- Do not make `.badge` interactive; it reports rather than acts, so it carries no hover, focus or pressed state.
- Do not signal state with the dot colour alone; a screen reader gets nothing from `.badge__dot`.
- Do not use `.badge` as a tag; a label with no state is `.chip`.
- Do not repaint `--badge-dot` to follow a theme; it is brand lime in both by design, and only the pill chrome flips.

## Example

```html
<span class="badge"><span class="badge__dot" aria-hidden="true"></span>Open to work</span>
```

## Look

- **Chips vs badges vs counters** resolve by job: a label is a chip, a status is a badge, a count is
  the carousel counter. A badge is read-only and never interactive; its dot stays lime in both themes
  but colour is never the only signal, every status also carries a word.

Values in braces, such as `{colors.border}`, are named on the foundation pages, starting with [Colour](../foundations/color.md); every token with its purpose is on [Tokens](../foundations/tokens.md).

## Recipe

The recipe from [DESIGN.md](../DESIGN.md), one entry per state. Names in braces resolve on the foundation pages.

```yaml
badge:
  backgroundColor: "transparent"
  textColor: "{colors.text-secondary}"
  border: "{structure.border-hairline}"
  typography: "{typography.label} mono, weight 500"
  rounded: "{rounded.full}"
  padding: "4px 12px"
  dot: "{colors.brand-lime} (6px, stays lime in both themes; the word carries meaning)"
```

## Classes

| Class | Kind | What it does | Tokens it reads |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.badge` | base | transparent, hairline border | `--badge-border`, `--badge-fg`, `--badge-font`, `--badge-font-size`, `--badge-font-weight`, `--badge-gap`, `--badge-icon-size`, `--badge-pad-x`, `--badge-pad-y`, `--badge-radius`, `--font-feature-mono` |
| `.badge__dot` | element | lime status dot; always pair it with a word, never colour alone | `--badge-dot`, `--badge-dot-size`, `--dot-radius` |

## Tokens

Every token the classes above read, as data from tokens.json: write `var(--name)`, never the raw value. A component token belongs to one component: change it to restyle that component and nothing else. A semantic token is a shared role; never change one for a single component. The three tiers: [Tokens](../foundations/tokens.md#three-tiers).

| Token | Tier | Value | What it is for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--badge-border` | Component | `#e4e4e7`; dark `#27272a`, from `--color-border` | Badge outline; hairline, auto-flips per theme. |
| `--badge-dot` | Component | `#d2ff37`, from `--brand-primary` | Status-dot fill; brand lime in both themes (the dot is decorative, the label carries the meaning). |
| `--badge-dot-size` | Component | `6px` | Status-dot diameter inside a badge. Component-level literal. |
| `--badge-fg` | Component | `#3f3f46`; dark `#a1a1aa`, from `--color-text-secondary` | Badge label and icon colour; quiet by design, auto-flips per theme. |
| `--badge-font` | Component | `"JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace`, from `--font-mono` | Badge label typeface (JetBrains Mono). |
| `--badge-font-size` | Component | `0.6875rem`, from `--text-label` | Badge label size. |
| `--badge-font-weight` | Component | `500`, from `--weight-medium` | Badge label weight. |
| `--badge-gap` | Component | `8px`, from `--space-200` | Space between a badge's dot or icon and its label. |
| `--badge-icon-size` | Component | `0.875rem`, from `--size-sm` | Leading icon footprint inside a badge (Lucide stroke icon). Sits on the --size-sm step of the size scale. |
| `--badge-pad-x` | Component | `12px`, from `--space-300` | Badge inline (left/right) padding; 12px. |
| `--badge-pad-y` | Component | `4px`, from `--space-100` | Badge block (top/bottom) padding; 4px. |
| `--badge-radius` | Component | `999px`, from `--radius-full` | Badge corner radius; full pill. |
| `--dot-radius` | Semantic | `999px`, from `--radius-full` | Circle geometry: dots, markers, slider thumbs, and drawn circles (the brand period, status dots, touch-target rings). Full by definition: a re-theme that softens buttons leaves a dot round, and the theme lab's corner tier squares it only when the whole system goes sharp (0 at sharp, full at soft and round). |
| `--font-feature-mono` | Semantic | `"zero" 1` | Switches on the slashed zero for every piece of mono text. |
